slides.title: Everyone left the meeting thinking **someone else** would do it.
paras: Notes like these record what was said. Not who's doing what, or by when.

cards.title: Notes → actions
cards.text: Turn these meeting notes into 3 sections: DECISIONS (what we agreed), ACTIONS (task, owner, deadline), OPEN QUESTIONS (not decided yet). If an owner or deadline is missing, write NOT SET. Don't guess. Notes: [PASTE]

slides.note: Leave out anything private: pay, health, HR issues.

messages.text:
**DECISIONS**
• 2 seasonal drinks on the holiday menu, not 4
• Deep clean Sat 2nd, everyone in at 8

ACTIONS
• Cost the 2 drinks: Jen, NOT SET
• New rota from Nov: Sam, NOT SET
• Availability to Sam: everyone, Fri
• Call dishwasher repair: you (note-taker), NOT SET

OPEN QUESTIONS
• Which 2 drinks? (gingerbread latte suggested)
• Who posts on social media? (Ali suggested, not agreed)

before.label: NOTES SAID

after.label: AI FLAGGED IT
after.text: OPEN: Who posts on social media? Ali suggested, not agreed.

slides.note: It didn't quietly hand the job to Ali. Unclear stays unclear until you decide.

caption:
How to turn messy meeting notes into action items with AI

Meeting over, notes full of "who? me I guess" and "maybe Ali?". Here's the fix:

"Turn these meeting notes into 3 sections: DECISIONS (what we agreed), ACTIONS (task, owner, deadline), OPEN QUESTIONS (not decided yet). If an owner or deadline is missing, write NOT SET. Don't guess. Notes: [PASTE]"

Then: "Now write a short message for the team chat: one line per action, owner first. Then list what's still open."

I tried it on example notes from a café team meeting. It pulled out 2 decisions, 4 actions with owners, and flagged what was never decided instead of guessing.

The routine: paste right after the meeting, fill in every NOT SET, send the recap, open the next meeting with it.

Leave out anything private: pay, health or HR issues.
